clue.text: Dejected when name is not top of the bill?

definitions.text: when name is not top of the bill
definitions.meaning: an actor whose name sits low down the cast list of a playbill is, read literally, down the cast

explanation.surface: An actor feels gloomy at being denied star billing on the poster.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: DOWN (not at the top) and CAST (the list of performers on a bill).
explanation.definitionFit: Being cast down is an old idiom for being in low spirits, the same as dejected.

clue.text: Dismal doctor takes a year off

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters of year are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy GP takes twelve months' leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like the doctor's leave, but it signals the anagram: EARY from YEAR follows DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull and depressing, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Precipitate drop of current — flaw later rectified

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A fault in the flow of water gets fixed afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rectified' turns FLAW and LATER, nine letters together, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a sheer, headlong plunge of a river's current over a cliff.

clue.text: A number take exam, naturally it's hard

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A number of pupils sit a test, which is naturally difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naturally it's hard' describes the stony skeleton built by sea creatures in reefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Reef material is a hard stony substance made naturally by tiny marine polyps.

clue.text: The class endlessly in riot carried out by schoolchildren

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion
endlessly says the final letter of class is dropped

explanation.surface: A class running wild, with schoolchildren carrying out the disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims class to CLAS; 'in riot' scrambles THE + CLAS into the answer. 'carried out by' is not a phrase here: the bag is carried by children.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is what pupils traditionally carry their books in.

clue.text: April's turning out to be springlike

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters of April's are turned into a fresh order

explanation.surface: April is proving to be a spring month after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'springlike' is not about the season: it means coiled like a spring. 'turning out' rearranges APRILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil, the shape of a wound metal spring, winds round and round in a helix.

clue.text: Cop in male form

indicators.note: form is used as a verb meaning shape, so the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A police officer who happens to be a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads 'Top', but the anagram needs COP: 'form' rearranges COP IN MALE, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A male officer of the law is a constable, the cop of the clue in a man's shape.

clue.text: Spanish wine and port provided with German agreement

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous Brazilian port, often shortened to Rio
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine is shipped through a harbour with German approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A red from northern Spain's best-known wine region, named after the region.

clue.text: It rarely turns out like this in books

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned around into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something rarely happens the way it does in novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges IT RARELY; the rest describes the answer as the quality of being found in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing and literature are what books contain, so bookish style is described by the answer.

clue.text: Whole eternity blown to bits

indicators.note: something blown to bits is shattered, so the letters of eternity are reassembled

explanation.surface: All of eternity is destroyed in an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something is all of it, the total sum.

clue.text: Approaching resort of St Malo

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters of St Malo are sorted again

explanation.surface: Drawing near to the Breton seaside town of Saint-Malo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' pretends to call St Malo a holiday town; read as re-sort, it signals the anagram of STMALO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly there, close to but not quite reaching something, is the sense shared.

clue.text: Food produced in layers

parts.note: layers here are hens that lay, not strata, and their output is the breakfast food

explanation.definitionFit: Hens kept for laying produce this food every day, so layers make it.

clue.text: Country river-a Russian river

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A rural setting where one river meets a Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective means of the countryside, as in country life.

clue.text: It raises the issue of a senior professorial post

definitions.meaning: issue means offspring, so this lifts a small child up to the table
a chair is a professorship, and a high one is senior

explanation.surface: A university appointment that brings up a contentious question.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall infant seat lifts a toddler, and a top academic chair is a lofty post.

clue.text: This young woman's rejection makes man angry

indicators.note: rejection is read as a throwing back, so the letters come out in reverse

parts.note: Les is a man's name
mad means angry

explanation.surface: A girl turns down a suitor and leaves him furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden in old romances is an unmarried girl, a young woman.

clue.text: Baseball fielder — in trunks and jumper?

parts.note: trunks are short trousers, shorts
a jumper (British for a sweater) is a top

explanation.surface: A baseball player dressed in bathing trunks and a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a pullover, a top.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the position between second and third base is a fielding post.

clue.text: University course remains chaotic

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters of remains are jumbled

explanation.surface: A university course stays in a state of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb with 'chaotic' its complement; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-group class for discussion at a college is a standard teaching unit.

clue.text: Men driven wild? Doesn't matter!

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the two words run riot

explanation.surface: Men have been driven crazy, but so what?
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive interjection telling someone to forget it is an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Front vehicle needs protection

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard is a protection

explanation.surface: The lead vehicle requires an escort.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading part of an army or movement is the front line.

clue.text: Everything considered, no-one is left in ignorance

definitions.meaning: taking everything into account, in total
read literally, every person has been informed

explanation.surface: When everything is weighed up, nobody remains uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in total, and literally says every person has been informed.

clue.text: Decline and fall

definitions.meaning: a decline is a decrease, as in prices
to fall is to come down

explanation.surface: The decline and fall of an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip in value and a plunge downward both describe a descent.

clue.text: Information a girl found in Switzerland

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Some news of a young woman tracked down in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information or facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on Lake Leman, it is located in the west of the Swiss Confederation.

clue.text: it may be checked for drink and meat around midnight

indicators.note: around says the drink and meat surround the letter between them

parts.note: gin is a drink
ham is a meat
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A drink and some meat consumed around midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked' means patterned in squares, not examined. 'midnight' gives G, the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton fabric woven in a squares pattern is the classic checked cloth.

clue.text: Animal has no end of courage in a melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused scuffle, so the letters are mixed up
has no end of means the final letter of courage is dropped

explanation.surface: A beast loses its nerve in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no end of' trims courage to COURAG, and 'in a melee' scrambles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wild cat of the Americas, also called puma or mountain lion.

clue.text: A spirited community? Surely not!

parts.note: spirited suggests lively, but a place populated only by spirits is deserted, the opposite of lively

explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement with no residents is said to be haunted by its past.

clue.text: An outdoor party is best

parts.note: out means outdoors, outside; the answer's letters also sit at the front of this word, a coincidence, since party supplies the last two letters
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A garden party beats all others.
explanation.walkthrough: Best is a verb here: to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone is to surpass them, a verb sense shared with the answer.

clue.text: Load the vehicle and leave

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
go means leave

explanation.surface: Pack up the car and set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight load carried on a ship or plane is its consignment.

clue.text: Hundred and four going round Greek island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters of four being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hundred and four people touring a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges FOUR into ORFU after C.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ionian holiday destination off the north-west coast of Greece.

clue.text: Sculpting statue, showing ingenuity

indicators.note: sculpting means reshaping, so the letters of statue are moulded anew

explanation.surface: Carving a statue displays great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and clever, quick to see an advantage: the sense of cunning ingenuity.

clue.text: How delightful — tea with best china

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
Ming porcelain is the finest Chinese china

explanation.surface: Tea served in the finest porcelain: how lovely!
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is old British slang for tea; Ming is the Chinese dynasty famed for porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of pleasure, often ironic, like lovely.

clue.text: Is listless, so prod into action

indicators.note: springing into action stirs the letters of so prod into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone flags, so a nudge is needed to get them going.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagging and flagging from tiredness describes a lack of energy.

clue.text: Burn slowly soon beginning to turn to dust

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of soon

parts.note: to moulder is to decay and crumble to dust

explanation.surface: Fire takes its time, and soon everything crumbles to dust.
explanation.definitionFit: To glow and burn without flame is a slow, smoky combustion.
